record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; the code and listed result files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README says the project replicates and extends the analysis to Qwen3.5-2B, and reports results from difference-in-means directions and projection ablation.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal and attack-success results for layer and layer-group ablations. It describes other result files, but their contents were not available for extraction.
record.test_reason: It applies difference-in-means directions with projection ablation to a new model, Qwen3.5-2B, which mixes linear and full attention. It reports refusal and attack-success rates after ablation. The recipe differs from the original in two ways. It computes a separate direction for each layer, and it hooks only the chosen layers' outputs instead of ablating one direction at every layer. So this is a new setting rather than a strict T1 replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README concludes that refusal in Qwen3.5-2B is concentrated in middle layers (6–14), especially linear-attention layers 9–10, rather than in the last layers. It reports that a single-layer ablation bypasses safety on 70% of prompts and that full-model ablation reaches 90%. It contrasts this with Qwen3.5-27B, where refusal sits in layers 48–63. It suggests that smaller models encode refusal differently and that relative position matters. It also reports that full-attention layers contribute no more than linear-attention layers.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes harmful-minus-safe mean directions and projection removal, but computes a separate direction per layer and reports layer and group ablations. The repository is a replication and extension project; its README says it applies the analysis to Qwen3.5-2B.
record.method_sensitivity: Ablation outcome differs by layer and layer group; the README reports stronger effects for middle layers than for layers 16–23.
record.problems: The README describes only 10 harmful/safe prompt pairs. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported, and no general capability evaluation is described. The listed result files were not read, so their contents cannot be checked.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows extracted from the listed JSON, image, or findings files because their contents were not included in the README and were not read.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; preservation of other abilities or harmless-prompt behaviour; a single shared direction ablated across all layers; per-layer results for the 19 layers not in the top-5 table.

missing.what: Per-layer ablation ASR for the remaining 19 layers; the README gives only the top 5 and says the rest are minimal.
Batch groups named in the pipeline but not reported in the README table (e.g. top_half).

record.verdict_notes: An unreviewed GitHub project with 10 prompt pairs, so each ASR step is one prompt. There is no uncertainty estimate, no control and no capability evaluation. Refusal is judged by keywords. The README wrongly attributes 'Abliteration' to Zou et al. 2023 and does not cite the original refusal-direction paper. The LoRA fine-tuning experiment is outside the claim and was not read. The 27B comparison is a cited external result, not a transfer test.

versions.untested_parts: The README reports removal tests, not direction addition or whether other abilities are preserved. It uses a separate harmful-minus-safe direction for each layer, rather than testing one shared direction ablated at every layer.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is reported; the described intervention is a forward hook on activations.
No jailbreak attack that suppresses the direction, or training against its ablation, is reported.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account is reported.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision is reported.
The README mentions a separate Qwen3.5-27B result from another source, but does not report a transfer test in this repository.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or training stages is reported.

relation.reason: Its own ablation results (ASR after projecting out DiM directions) bear directly on whether ablation removes refusal.

tranche.reason: It applies DiM direction ablation to a new hybrid linear/full-attention model and reports refusal/ASR. The method differs from the original: one direction per layer, no single selected direction, layer-restricted ablations and keyword detection. So T1 (the reader's first call) is too strong and T3 fits.

source_check.notes: The text is the README only (no results JSON or findings.md). ASR appears to be scored by keyword matching (config.py has 'refusal keywords') on the same 10 dangerous prompts used to fit the directions, with no held-out set, no controls and no capability check. The README credits abliteration to Zou et al. 2023 and does not cite Arditi. The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1/l2 follow the pack's order.

statements.correction: Qwen3.5-2B, per-layer DiM directions, 10 dangerous prompts: top five single layers (9, 10, 6, 8, 11) give ASR 70/70/50/40/30%; last_8 (16–23) 0%; full_model (0–23) 90%; baseline refuses 100%.
statements.problem: Numbers right. Minor precision issue: 30–70% covers only the five top-ranked single layers the README lists (6, 8, 9, 10, 11). Other middle layers (e.g. 7, 12–14) are not reported and are presumably lower.

statements.correction: Qwen3.5-2B: per-layer DiM directions ablated at all 24 layers give 90% ASR (baseline 100% refusal); single layers at most 70%; layer groups 60–70%; layers 16–23 0%. A single direction across all layers was not tested.
statements.problem: 'Needs separate per-layer directions' is not shown. The study only ever uses per-layer directions and never tests one global direction applied at all layers. What it does show is that the set of layers ablated matters, not per-layer versus single direction.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The interventions increase ASR, but do not fully remove refusal; results also vary substantially by layer group, including no reported ASR increase for layers 16–23 alone (r1–r9).
